newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates firm ahead of bill tender.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates firm ahead of bill tender.

text.p: Interbank rates were generally firmer on expectations of a further liquidity tightness after a 500-million ringgit Bank Negara bills issue on Tuesday, dealers said.
Results of the bills tender will be announced later today with payment on Wednesday.

"Rates are firming back ahead of the payment," said a dealer with a Malaysian bank. "But I still think this will be temporary and rates should come off again as there are few maturities (of Bank Negara bills) coming."
One- and two-week money were at 10.0/15.0 percent against 8.0/9.5 percent on Monday.
One-month money was at 9.0/9.5 percent and three- and six-month at 8.0/8.5 percent. They were all quoted at 7.5/8.0 percent on Monday.
Dealers said the overnight rate was also expected to stay firm on Tuesday. It traded between 13 and 20 percent on Monday.

The rise in interbank rates started last Thursday after Bank Negara intervened aggressively in the foreign exchange market to stem the slide of the ringgit. The central bank was said to have sold around $1 billion.
The intervention drained liquidity from the system, causing the market to be short and interbank rates to rise to unusually high levels.
Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange fell, losing some of their recent gains.
At 0330 GMT, the benchmark three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) June contract was down four points to 92.48, or an implied yield of 7.52 percent.
September was down two to 92.51, or 7.49 percent.
